method: Arb interval Hessian on an exact rank-two Kossakowski amplitude chart, plus analytic Frechet norm bounds for the third derivative

rank_two_chart.kossakowski_matrix: C=z z^dagger+w w^dagger, hence C is PSD and rank at most two
rank_two_chart.local_coverage: For a nearby rank-at-most-two PSD C with a simple leading eigenvalue, choose orthogonal spectral amplitudes z,w; jump phase and fixed-basis rephasing put z on the stated transverse slice, and z_z nonzero gives the displayed eta coordinates.
rank_two_chart.ball_definition: native coordinates x=x_*+B y with B the recorded fixed whitening matrix and ||y||_2 no larger than the certified radius; interval work encloses the containing coordinate cube |y_i|<=radius

augmented_support.stationarity: The interval-Newton equations make all gauge-slice derivatives of b-lambda*a vanish at x_*; eta enters through D[w] quadratically, and a=1/2, hence grad G=0.

uniform_certificate.conclusion: Every chart point in the Euclidean y-ball with a=1/2 has b>=b_*; strict inequality holds away from gauge-equivalent representations of the root.

third_frechet_taylor_bound.inequality: G(y)-G(0)>=mu*||y||_2^2/2-L3*||y||_2^3/6, using the recorded Frobenius bound L3 for D^3G on the containing cube
third_frechet_taylor_bound.note: The direct interval-Hessian radius is stronger; this separate conservative radius records an explicit third-Frechet/Lipschitz Taylor control.

limitations: The certificate is local in an explicitly normalized chart and covers rank-at-most-two Kossakowski matrices near the simple rank-one root. It does not cover rank-three dissipators, distant generators, unbounded rates/times, prove that b_* is the global restricted minimum, or identify the true Q2 boundary.
